keys.beat: Odysseus wakes, smells the meat, and condemns the act, but the crew feasts for six days.
keys.text: When I had got some way down towards my ship I began to smell hot roast meat, so I groaned out a prayer to the immortal gods... for six days my men kept driving in the best cows and feasting upon them.

keys.beat: On the seventh day the wind falls and the ship leaves Thrinacia.
keys.text: When Jove the son of Saturn had added a seventh day, the fury of the gale abated; we therefore went on board, raised our masts, spread sail, and put out to sea.

keys.beat: Zeus gathers a black cloud and strikes the mast with lightning.
keys.text: Jove thundered and hurled a thunderbolt upon the ship, which reeled beneath the blow, and was filled with fire and brimstone.

keys.beat: The ship shatters and every crewman drowns; Odysseus lashes keel and mast together.
keys.text: The men all fell into the sea; they were carried about in the water round the ship, looking like so many sea-gulls... I lashed the mast and keel together, and getting astride of them was carried wherever the winds chose to take me.

keys.beat: Driven back to Charybdis, he hangs from the fig tree until the timbers reemerge, then drifts alone to Calypso.
keys.text: I sprang up to the fig tree, and clung to it like a bat... I clung on till she should spew up my raft again... I let go with my hands and feet, and fell heavily into the sea, hard by my raft.
